title: README.md claims an issue is fixed, but it's still open
author: off-by-one
description: Reads README.md's own text for a real GitHub closing-keyword claim (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses) and cross-checks it against the live issue tracker. The issue-side twin of readme-claims-open-milestone -- README's own claims-X family had a milestone leg and no issue leg, unlike the release and tweet families, which both carry all three.
confidence_notes: Deliberately NOT age-gated, the same reasoning readme-claims-open-milestone already gave for its own README read. A GetFileContents read of README.md returns current text, not a change history, so there is no per-claim timestamp to weigh a staleness window against -- and no race to guard against either: a README is read live, right now, so a claim it currently makes and the issue's currently-open state are both true at the same instant the scan runs. Flat 0.85 on every surfaced claim; a claim naming a nonexistent issue, or one that is genuinely closed, is excluded at 0.0, named not hidden.
